comment: Achievable synovial/extracellular [KPV] per dosing route. The pore equilibrates INTRACELLULAR [KPV] to this EXTRACELLULAR (synovial) value, so C_ext per route is the master input for the flux-sufficiency (A1) verdict. IA is computed directly (dose / synovial volume). SC and oral are design-space PK assumptions (KPV systemic PK is not well characterized) and are flagged as such.

intra_articular.derivation: Dose / synovial fluid volume. Central: 0.2 mg KPV / 342.43 g/mol = 0.584 umol into 2 mL normal knee synovial volume = 292 uM. Range: 0.1-1 mg into 2-20 mL (normal-to-large-effusion). 1 mg/2 mL = 1460 uM; 0.1 mg/20 mL = 15 uM. Gout-flare joints (podagra MTP1 ~0.5-1 mL; knee effusion up to 10-50 mL) bracket this. All values are >> the 10 nM IC50 and near-or-above the PepT1 Km (160-700 uM), so PepT1 SATURATES in healthy cells at IA doses.

subcutaneous.derivation: NAMED PK ASSUMPTION. 0.5 mg SC, bioavailability >80% (kpv-peptide.md). Peak plasma ~= dose/Vd with Vd ~ extracellular fluid (~15 L for a hydrophilic peptide): 0.5 mg/15 L = 33 ng/mL = ~0.10 uM peak plasma. Synovial fluid is a plasma ultrafiltrate; small-peptide synovial:plasma partition ~0.3-0.5 -> ~0.03-0.05 uM synovial peak. KPV plasma half-life is short (peptide, rapid clearance) so time-averaged synovial level is lower; central 0.030 uM (30 nM). Range 3-200 nM. This is ONLY ~3x the 10 nM IC50 -- a thin margin.

oral.derivation: NAMED PK ASSUMPTION. Oral KPV bioavailability is 'low but sufficient' and is optimized for LOCAL GUT action (PepT1 in enterocytes); systemic delivery is poor. Systemic plasma from oral KPV is estimated 10-100x below SC -> synovial [KPV] ~0.1-3 nM. Central 1 nM (0.1x IC50). Oral is a gut-luminal / intestinal-uricolysis route, not a systemic-joint route; included to show it fails the joint-delivery bar on absolute concentration.
